title: Lead RRP scope and definitions practice questions
description: Free Lead RRP practice questions on scope and definitions in 40 CFR 745.80-745.88. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: What does 745.80 say Subpart E is meant to ensure for owners and occupants of target housing and child-occupied facilities?

options.A: That they pay for any renovation of their property through a certified firm
options.B: That they test their own paint before hiring a firm
options.C: That they receive information on lead-based paint hazards before these renovations begin
options.D: That they sign the firm's certification application

questions.explanation: One purpose of the subpart is to ensure that "Owners and occupants of target housing and child-occupied facilities receive information on lead-based paint hazards before these renovations begin".

questions.question: Under 745.81(a), where are the Subpart E training, certification and accreditation requirements and work practice standards applicable?

options.A: In any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program authorized under subpart Q
options.B: Only in States that have their own authorized renovation program
options.C: Only on Indian Tribal lands
options.D: Only in housing owned by the Federal Government

questions.explanation: They "are applicable in any State or Indian Tribal area that does not have a renovation program that is authorized under subpart Q of this part."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.81, Effective dates (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: On or after April 22, 2010, what does 745.81(a)(2)(ii) bar a firm from doing in target housing or child-occupied facilities without EPA certification under 745.89, unless an exception in 745.82(a) or (c) applies?

options.A: Applying to EPA for certification
options.B: Buying EPA recognized test kits
options.C: Hiring an inspector or risk assessor to make a written determination
options.D: Performing, offering, or claiming to perform renovations

questions.explanation: "On or after April 22, 2010, no firm may perform, offer, or claim to perform renovations without certification from EPA under § 745.89 in target housing or child-occupied facilities, unless the renovation qualifies for one of the exceptions identified in § 745.82(a) or (c)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.81, Effective dates (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Exceptions: determinations, test kits and paint chips
questions.question: For the written determination exception in 745.82(a)(1), who must make the determination that the affected components are free of lead paint at the regulated level?

options.A: The firm's owner, after a visual check
options.B: An inspector or risk assessor certified under 745.226 or a State or Tribal certification program authorized under 745.324
options.C: The property owner, based on the year of construction
options.D: The local building department

questions.explanation: The determination must be "made by an inspector or risk assessor (certified pursuant to either Federal regulations at § 745.226 or a State or Tribal certification program authorized pursuant to § 745.324)".

questions.topic: Exceptions: determinations, test kits and paint chips
questions.question: Besides the written determination itself, what else does 745.82(a)(1) require for that exception to apply?

options.A: The determination must be posted at the entrance to the work area
options.B: The firm performing the renovation has obtained a copy of the determination
options.C: EPA must countersign the determination
options.D: The occupants must sign a copy of the determination

questions.explanation: The exception applies "where the firm performing the renovation has obtained a copy of the determination."

questions.topic: Exceptions: determinations, test kits and paint chips
questions.question: Under the test kit exception in 745.82(a)(2), what must the certified renovator test with an EPA recognized test kit, following the kit manufacturer's instructions?

options.A: Each component affected by the renovation
options.B: One component chosen at random in each room
options.C: Only components with visibly peeling paint
options.D: Only the exterior components of the building

questions.explanation: The certified renovator "has tested each component affected by the renovation"; for components that make up an integrated whole, only one need be tested "unless the individual components appear to have been repainted or refinished separately."

questions.topic: Exceptions: determinations, test kits and paint chips
questions.question: Under the paint chip exception in 745.82(a)(3), after a certified renovator collects a paint chip sample from each painted component affected, who must determine that the samples are free of lead paint at the regulated level?

options.A: The firm's own office staff
options.B: The paint manufacturer
options.C: The local building department
options.D: A laboratory recognized by EPA pursuant to section 405(b) of TSCA as capable of analyzing lead compounds in paint chip samples

questions.explanation: The determination is made by "a laboratory recognized by EPA pursuant to section 405(b) of TSCA as being capable of performing analyses for lead compounds in paint chip samples".

questions.question: What example of a sudden, unexpected event does 745.82(b) give when it describes emergency renovations?

options.A: A scheduled kitchen remodel
options.B: Routine repainting when a tenant moves out
options.C: Non-routine failures of equipment
options.D: A planned window replacement program

questions.explanation: Emergency renovations "result from a sudden, unexpected event (such as non-routine failures of equipment) that, if not immediately attended to, presents a safety or public health hazard, or threatens equipment and/or property with significant damage."

questions.question: An emergency repair (not interim controls) leaves no time to post warning signs or set up containment under 745.85. How far does the 745.82(b) exemption from those requirements reach?

options.A: To the extent necessary to respond to the emergency
options.B: To the whole job, including the cleaning and cleaning verification afterward
options.C: Only until EPA approves a written waiver for the job
options.D: Only to jobs in buildings with no child under age 6

questions.explanation: Emergency renovations other than interim controls are exempt from these requirements "to the extent necessary to respond to the emergency." They "are not exempt from the cleaning requirements of § 745.85(a)(5)" or the cleaning verification requirements of § 745.85(b).

questions.question: Besides unplanned work after a sudden, unexpected event, which activity does 745.82(b) say is also an emergency renovation?

options.A: Any renovation in a vacant dwelling unit
options.B: A renovation a tenant has requested in writing
options.C: Repainting done to prepare a unit for sale
options.D: Interim controls performed in response to an elevated blood lead level in a resident child

questions.explanation: "Interim controls performed in response to an elevated blood lead level in a resident child are also emergency renovations."

questions.question: In a public or commercial building that contains a child-occupied facility, which common areas does the child-occupied facility encompass under 745.83?

options.A: Every common area in the building, including hallways and garages
options.B: Only those common areas that are routinely used by children under age 6, such as restrooms and cafeterias
options.C: No common areas at all
options.D: Only the building's parking areas

questions.explanation: It "encompasses only those common areas that are routinely used by children under age 6, such as restrooms and cafeterias." Areas children "only pass through, such as hallways, stairways, and garages are not included."

questions.question: A day care center leases space in a commercial building, and a firm will repaint the building's outside walls. Which exterior sides are part of the child-occupied facility under 745.83?

options.A: All exterior sides of the building
options.B: Only the side with the main entrance
options.C: Only the exterior sides immediately adjacent to the child-occupied facility or the common areas routinely used by children under age 6
options.D: No exterior sides

questions.explanation: It "encompasses only the exterior sides of the building that are immediately adjacent to the child-occupied facility or the common areas routinely used by children under age 6."

questions.topic: Renovation and minor repair and maintenance
questions.question: Under 745.83, how is a renovation performed to convert a building, or part of a building, into target housing or a child-occupied facility treated?

options.A: It is a renovation under Subpart E
options.B: It is new construction and outside Subpart E
options.C: It is always treated as an abatement
options.D: It is a minor repair and maintenance activity

questions.explanation: "A renovation performed for the purpose of converting a building, or part of a building, into target housing or a child-occupied facility is a renovation under this subpart."

questions.topic: Renovation and minor repair and maintenance
questions.question: When painted components, or portions of them, are removed, how does 745.83 say the amount of painted surface disturbed is measured?

options.A: Only the area of paint that is cracked or peeling
options.B: Only the length of the saw cut
options.C: Half of the surface area removed
options.D: The entire surface area removed

questions.explanation: "When removing painted components, or portions of painted components, the entire surface area removed is the amount of painted surface disturbed."

questions.topic: Renovation and minor repair and maintenance
questions.question: A firm does two small jobs in the same room two weeks apart, and neither is an emergency renovation. How does the 745.83 definition of minor repair and maintenance activities treat them?

options.A: Each job is judged on its own, whatever the time between them
options.B: Only the larger of the two jobs is counted
options.C: They must be considered the same job for deciding whether the work is a minor repair and maintenance activity
options.D: The second job is exempt because the first was already reviewed

questions.explanation: "Jobs, other than emergency renovations, performed in the same room within the same 30 days must be considered the same job for the purpose of determining whether the job is a minor repair and maintenance activity."

questions.question: A county government agency asks whether it can be a "firm" under the 745.83 definition. What does the definition say?

options.A: No; only private businesses can be firms
options.B: Yes; a Federal, State, Tribal, or local government agency is included in the definition of firm
options.C: Only if the agency holds a State contractor's license
options.D: No; government agencies fall only under the definition of "person"

questions.explanation: "Firm means a company, partnership, corporation, sole proprietorship or individual doing business, association, or other business entity; a Federal, State, Tribal, or local government agency; or a nonprofit organization."

questions.question: Under the 745.83 definition of "training hour", which of these counts toward the at least 50 minutes of actual learning?

options.A: Travel time to the training site
options.B: Meal breaks during the course day
options.C: Time spent registering before class begins
options.D: Demonstrations and hands-on experience

questions.explanation: "Training hour means at least 50 minutes of actual learning, including, but not limited to, time devoted to lecture, learning activities, small group activities, demonstrations, evaluations, and hands-on experience."

questions.question: Under the 745.83 definition of "wet mopping system", which feature does the device have?

options.A: A reservoir for cleaning solution and a built-in mechanism for distributing or spraying the solution onto a floor
options.B: A HEPA filter as the last filtration stage
options.C: A beater bar that loosens carpet fibers
options.D: A cleaning verification card mounted on the handle

questions.explanation: A wet mopping system is a device with "A long handle, a mop head designed to be used with disposable absorbent cleaning pads, a reservoir for cleaning solution, and a built-in mechanism for distributing or spraying the cleaning solution onto a floor, or a method of equivalent efficacy."

questions.question: Under 745.88(b), apart from the kits recognized under paragraph (a), what must happen before EPA recognizes a test kit?

options.A: The manufacturer lists the kit on its own website
options.B: A State building code office approves the kit
options.C: The kit is tested through EPA's Environmental Technology Verification Program or other equivalent EPA approved testing program
options.D: A certified renovator files a report of field use

questions.explanation: "No other test kits will be recognized until they are tested through EPA's Environmental Technology Verification Program or other equivalent EPA approved testing program."

questions.question: What negative response criterion does 745.88(c)(1) set for paint containing lead at or above the regulated level?

options.A: A demonstrated probability (with 90% confidence) of a negative response less than or equal to 20% of the time
options.B: A demonstrated probability (with 95% confidence) of a negative response less than or equal to 5% of the time
options.C: A demonstrated probability (with 80% confidence) of a negative response less than or equal to 50% of the time
options.D: A demonstrated probability (with 99% confidence) of a negative response less than or equal to 1% of the time

questions.explanation: For paint at or above 1.0 mg/cm2 or 0.5% by weight, the criterion is "a demonstrated probability (with 95% confidence) of a negative response less than or equal to 5% of the time."
